evidence: Cic. Planc. 94: nāvem secundīs ventīs cursum tenentem (Lewis & Short s.v. secundus)
Caes. BG 4.23: ventum et aestum ūnō tempore nactus secundum (Lewis & Short)
Ov. M. 13.418: flātūque secundō (Lewis & Short s.v. flātus)
terms.comment: Secundus is “following”, from sequor: the wind that follows the ship. The head wind is ventus adversus.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
